package_info.why_malicious: This report does not analyze a specific malicious package, but provides macro-level evidence that malicious open-source packages are a rapidly growing threat. It highlights a 1300% increase in malicious packages over three years, with attackers exploiting open-source repositories (npm, PyPI, RubyGems) to distribute malware, steal secrets, and compromise software supply chains. The report also details real-world incidents (e.g., 3CX) where attackers inserted malicious code into legitimate software via supply chain compromise.

execution_context.file_location: modified open-source files within the 3CX Desktop App build pipeline

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code inserted into standard open-source files, executed as part of the 3CX Desktop App build process (exact code not shown in report).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build-time, the code is injected into the application, resulting in the distribution of a trojanized desktop app to customers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modification of standard open-source files in the build pipeline to insert malicious code is a hallmark of supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build processes should not alter trusted open-source dependencies to include unauthorized code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code signing or telemetry additions, but only with full transparency and review.
key_indicators: Unexpected changes to open-source files in build artifacts
Malicious code present in distributed binaries
Lack of detection prior to release

execution_context.file_location: malicious packages uploaded to npm, PyPI, RubyGems

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Infostealer, backdoor, or protestware code embedded in open-source packages (exact code not shown in report).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time or import-time, the code exfiltrates secrets, credentials, or environment variables to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Open-source packages should not exfiltrate secrets or perform unauthorized network communication.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or transmit sensitive data without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting, but only with user opt-in and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Network requests to untrusted domains during install/import
Access to environment variables or credential files
Obfuscated or hidden code in package scripts

execution_context.file_location: leaked secrets within open-source package repositories (e.g., PyPI, npm)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Leaked API keys, tokens, and credentials (e.g., OpenAI, AWS, Google, GitHub) embedded in package code or configuration files.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, exposed secrets can be used by attackers to access cloud resources, APIs, or sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Secrets should never be hardcoded or published in public repositories.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Best practices dictate secrets are managed securely and never exposed in code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; secrets exposure is always a security risk.
key_indicators: Presence of API keys or tokens in public code
Secrets for high-value services (OpenAI, AWS, Google, GitHub)
No access controls or secret management

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads or modifies open-source packages to include malicious code or secrets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to developers and end users via trusted package managers.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes during build, install, or runtime, exfiltrating secrets or providing backdoor access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers gain access to sensitive data, cloud resources, or user environments.

attack_chain.action: Leaked secrets are harvested and abused by attackers for further compromise or lateral movement.
attack_chain.leads_to: Broader compromise of organizational assets, data theft, or service abuse.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during package install or import
Access to environment variables or credential files by package scripts
Presence of hardcoded secrets or API keys in public repositories
Modification of standard open-source files in build pipelines
file_indicators: setup.py, package.json, or other manifest files with obfuscated or suspicious scripts
Presence of secrets in code or configuration files
Unexpected changes to open-source dependencies in build artifacts
network_indicators: Outbound connections to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains during install/import
Exfiltration of environment variables or credential data
Use of webhook.site, pastebin, or similar data collection endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor package installation and import processes for unexpected network activity or access to sensitive files. Scan code and configuration files for hardcoded secrets or API keys. Use software composition analysis and binary diffing tools to detect unauthorized changes to open-source dependencies. Implement runtime monitoring to detect exfiltration attempts and unauthorized access to environment variables or credentials.
